eli: Quick heads-up — running a repeat of last night's replay harness showed a weird perf regression at ~60s into long-context runs. p95 TTFT jumped ~30%.
maria: ugh. same kernel selection/quant path as before?
eli: yes, same 8-bit path. suspecting batching + KV cache interaction when prefix hits are >70% and batch sizes spike.
sam: can you paste the profiling snippet?
eli: sure — here's the hot trace around the spike:
```
[2025-11-08T03:14:12Z] kernel_select: aten_gemm_fast (chosen)
[2025-11-08T03:14:12Z] kv_cache_lookup: 12.4ms (high hit-rate)
[2025-11-08T03:14:12Z] batch_concat: 42.8ms (variance + queuing)
[2025-11-08T03:14:12Z] attention_kernel_switch: fallback to generic_mm
[2025-11-08T03:14:12Z] token_emit: 2.0ms
```
jen: attention_kernel_switch fallback is red flag. is that due to sequence length variance in batch?
maria: probably — when cached KV lengths vary we pad. padding causes aten_gemm_fast to be inapplicable for some shards so runtime falls back.
eli: right. hypothesis: our batching heuristic coalesces requests aggressively to optimize token throughput (TPOT/QPS), but that increases sequence-length heterogeneity and triggers kernel fallbacks, spiking tail latency (TTFT p95/p99).
lina: did the replay harness use synthetic burst profiles or real traces? that matters for repro.
eli: replay harness — we used customer session traces with realistic prefix caching distribution (median prefix 120 tokens, 75th pct hit-rate 72%). also ran a synthetic peak test that didn't show the regression because synthetic traffic had uniform seq lengths.
sam: ok so apples-to-apples: we need a controlled replay with two axes: prefix_hit_rate and seq_length_variance. run grid: hit-rate [30, 50, 70, 90], variance low/med/high. measure TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT, goodput, and kernel fallback counts.
maria: agree. also add a metric for "kernel_switch_rate" (switches per 10k tokens) and "pad_overhead_pct" (extra tokens due to padding / total).
jen: what about KV cache behavior — are we clearing stale entries or merging shards incorrectly? any evictions during run?
eli: no evictions. KV hit stats stable. The weird thing is latency correlates with a burst of batch size 16->32 within one GPU shard. When that happens, combined seq variance jumps and kernel switch events spike.
perf-bot: Regression alert: CI-replay failed on long-context suite (TTFT p95 +28% vs baseline) — link: https://perf.redwood/compare/1859/1858
lina: thanks perf-bot. For next step I'll spin up the harness with the suggested grid and add kernel-level tracing (cuda kernel names + macro op counts). also enable per-request token timestamps so we can compute per-request TTFT and align with when padding occurred.
sam: temp mitigation: reduce max batch coalescing window from 15ms -> 5ms for long-context models or disable aggressive pad-coalescing when prefix_hit_rate > 60%. worth A/B testing.
maria: let's also add an apples-to-apples experiment comparing: (A) replay with original scheduling, (B) scheduling with smaller coalescing window, (C) scheduling + dynamic kernel pinning (force aten_gemm variant by splitting batches by seq length). measure p95/p99 and goodput loss.
jen: what thresholds for acceptable trade-offs? Ops wants p95 < 1200ms and goodput drop < 8% for the dedicated tier.
eli: noted. I'll run the grid and post a short summary with CSV attached. tentative timeline: 2 runs tonight (~3 hours) and a deeper run tomorrow across full model set.
lina: quick note — include a column for "replay fidelity" (percentage of original timing preserved) so we can sanity-check synthetic vs replay differences.
sam: perfect. If we confirm kernel fallback is the root cause, we should add a runtime heuristic: detect upcoming fallback risk and split batches proactively by seq-length buckets (cheap O(1) per-request).
maria: agree. small follow-up: capture a few raw protobuf request examples from the replay that hit fallback so we can re-run in a unit test harness.
eli: will do. posting initial CSV when the first grid finishes (~00:40 UTC). thanks all :thumbsup:
